first.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous pressure: competitive pricing threat to SMB segment, activation decline (-6%), and onboarding decline (-4%). Memory_73 (promotional pricing effectiveness for price-sensitive SMB) directly addresses the immediate competitive threat and revenue defense. Memory_86 (onboarding simplification lifting adoption) supports the onboarding decline but is secondary to stopping current churn. Verifying memory_73 is critical because promotional pricing carries downstream risk—unsustainable margin pressure and potential brand positioning damage—and needs confirmation that SMB segment economics remain healthy under pricing pressure. Memory_86 verification ensures onboarding simplification remains our fallback if pricing proves counterproductive. Activation messaging (memory_91) and referral incentives (memory_57) are lower-leverage given the competitive and engagement headwinds. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) doesn't address SMB churn. Promotional pricing as a standard experiment targets the most immediate threat while preserving optionality to layer onboarding improvements if activation trends don't improve post-pricing intervention.

final.rationale: Archive verification reveals critical finding: memory_73's promotional pricing showed +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue but -12% 30-day retention with poor renewal cycle survival. This directly contradicts sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective and invalidates promotional pricing as viable response to competitive pressure. Memory_86 verification confirms onboarding simplification is durable: +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, +3% retention. Given simultaneous activation (-6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) declines, the verified onboarding lever offers genuine ROI without margin degradation or cohort quality deterioration. This addresses root cause of engagement drop rather than masking it with unsustainable pricing. Referral incentives and activation messaging are secondary tactics best deployed after stabilizing onboarding. Enterprise sales assist doesn't solve SMB segment erosion. The promotional pricing trap—winning customers who don't stay—would compound our revenue problem at renewal. Simplify onboarding restores the completion funnel, improves time-to-value, and preserves retention quality.
